facts.text: After the troll is killed, the troll and the sword disappear, and eastward passage becomes accessible.
A stairway at the north end leads downward.
The reservoir cannot be crossed directly because it is too deep and wide; paths lead east and west, with a steep southwest route along a chasm.
The stream emerges from an opening too small for the player to enter.
The room contains empty tool chests, a wrench, a toothpaste-like tube, and a screwdriver; a thief carrying a large bag is associated with this area.
The thief is hostile and can kill the player when attacked with the sword.
A sword attack is not necessarily safe against every hostile character; attacking the thief caused immediate defeat and death.
Tested (confirmed): It blocks passage and must be defeated to reach the underground passages. -> Repeatedly killing the troll with the sword defeats it and permits eastward progress.
Tested (confirmed): A lamp may illuminate the dark staircase area, but none was available in this route. -> The brass lantern permits safe travel up the dark staircase into the attic.

Tested (confirmed): A hostile creature kills players who travel through darkness without adequate light. -> The dark staircase area is dangerous without adequate light, while the lit lantern enabled passage.
The gallery contains a painting of unparalleled beauty on its far wall; it may be an interactable object or treasure.
The studio contains a paper that identifies the player as the owner of ZORK I: The Great Underground Empire.
The dam lobby contains guidebooks and a matchbook whose cover says 'Visit Beautiful FCD#3'.
The dam has a scramble-down route leading to the Dam Base, and the river Frigid flows beside the base.
Deep Canyon has east, northwest, and southwest passages, plus a stairway leading down to the Loud Room.
The Loud Room contains a platinum bar, but taking or examining it only produces 'bar bar ...'.
The brass lantern's light steadily dims during extended activity; near the end it is nearly out and insufficient to protect against darkness.
Repeated north/south movement does not discover a route through the beach area; the tight west passage remains inaccessible.
Death occurred after the lantern became nearly exhausted and the player continued moving in the area; a grue then appeared and devoured the player.
Rule: A lantern is a temporary light source that becomes dimmer with continued use and can eventually be inadequate for dark-area survival.
Rule: Insufficient light in an underground or dark environment can lead to death by a grue.
Rule: Some apparent exits or passages require an object-specific interaction rather than ordinary movement.
Rule: Room descriptions may omit previously encountered objects or details when revisiting a room.
Rule: Score increases when major exploration or blocker-clearing milestones are achieved.
The maintenance room's rising water level advances over time and after actions; pressing blue starts a leak, yellow increases the level, and red turns on lights while the level continues rising.
The pile of plastic does not reveal anything special when examined.
The wrench can be taken after reducing inventory load, but later dropping and retaking items while the water rises can lead to drowning.
Moving south from the dam enters an unlit area; returning north without adequate light can result in death by a grue.
Taking the painting awards points.
Killing the troll with repeated sword attacks awards points when eastward access is opened.
Rule: Carrying too many objects prevents taking another object until inventory weight is reduced.
Rule: Entering an unlit dark area can lead to grue death, including when attempting to retreat.
Tested (confirmed): It may be collectible text or a humorous reward with no mechanical use. -> The studio paper is collectible and can be read; it identifies the player as the owner of ZORK I.
Tested (confirmed): A weapon used to defeat underground enemies. -> The elvish sword defeats the troll after repeated attacks and enables access eastward.
After the troll is defeated, the bloody axe remains and can be taken; examining it reveals nothing special.
The thief can appear in the Maintenance Room and steal possessions when the player handles objects nearby; he then leaves carrying his large bag.
The studio chimney cannot be climbed while carrying objects; when empty-handed, attempting to climb produces 'Going up empty-handed is a bad idea' rather than immediate ascent.
The gallery painting can be taken for points, but it is not present in the gallery after being dropped elsewhere.
The studio can contain objects carried or dropped by the player; revisiting it showed the painting, axe, lantern, manual, matchbook, bottle, and other items.
A light source cannot be turned on when the player cannot see because the surrounding area is too dark.
Rule: Inventory load can prevent taking objects or performing movement-based actions.
Rule: Dropping or leaving objects in a room allows them to be encountered there later.
Rule: Darkness can prevent ordinary actions and can cause death unless adequate light is available.
Tested (confirmed): It may be a weapon or useful tool after the troll is defeated. -> The axe is a takeable object left by the troll, but no special function was observed.
Tested (confirmed): A junction leading to the dam and canyon routes. -> The explored underground junction connects reservoir, dam, and canyon routes.
Opening the matchbook reveals that it contains five matches; lighting it starts one match burning, but dropping the lantern causes the match to go out.
The water level rises after actions and can reach waist height; the thief may appear there carrying a large bag.
Dropping many carried objects allows the previously too-heavy painting to be taken, awarding points.
The north and west exits from the gallery lead into unlit dark places; ordinary actions there fail because it is too dark to see.
The platinum bar cannot be acted on usefully by taking or examining it; both commands produce only 'bar bar ...'.
The guidebooks can be read, but the attempted page-selection commands using 'second', '2nd', or 'page 2' do not work.
The east exit leads to the Loud Room, while the south exit leads to a Narrow Passage; some other exits are blocked.
Carrying too many objects can prevent taking an object, and dropping carried objects reduces the load enough to take it.
A lit lantern does not illuminate a room after it has been dropped; attempting to light it in darkness fails because the player cannot see.
Entering darkness without an already usable light source can cause grue death, including when attempting to move back or perform actions there.
Rule: Inventory weight can block taking objects until enough items are dropped.
Rule: Darkness prevents ordinary interaction and can kill the player without an active light source.

Tested (confirmed): It may provide matches or a clue connected to the dam and possibly serve as a light-related tool. -> The matchbook contains matches and can light a match, but the transcript does not show it providing sustained area illumination.
The screwdriver can be taken after reducing inventory load; taking it while carrying the painting and lantern was too heavy.
The water level rises with time and actions even when the player does not press a water-control button.
The west and south exits from the dam lead into unlit areas; returning north from the southern dark area without a light causes grue death.
Dropping the lantern in the Maintenance Room leaves it there, and the lantern is visible when returning to that room.
The southern crawlway from the cellar leads to East of Chasm.
Rule: Actions can advance a rising water hazard in the Maintenance Room, including examination and inventory attempts.
Rule: Entering a dark area without an active light is dangerous, and retreating from it may still result in grue death.

The west exit from the Troll Room leads into a maze; repeated exploration encountered multiple indistinguishable passages and dead ends, and a downward route warned that returning upward would be impossible.
The Loud Room connects east to Damp Cave and contains a large platinum bar on the ground.
The cave's southern crack is too narrow for the player to enter.
The beach is a narrow north-south strip with no usable route west, east, up, down, or diagonally; the west passage cannot be entered normally.
Remaining in the beach area while carrying the brass lantern eventually exhausts it; when it became nearly out, retreating north led to grue death.
The lantern's light is consumed by movement and eventually becomes inadequate, even when it is carried and providing light.
Dropping the lantern removes its useful carried light; picking it up again is possible if inventory capacity permits.
The sword's glow can cease during underground exploration; examining it afterward does not reveal a special property.
Rule: Extended movement and activity can consume a carried light source until dark-area travel becomes unsafe.
Rule: A route may be described as present but still require an object-specific action rather than ordinary movement.
Rule: Dropping objects reduces inventory load, while taking objects can fail when the inventory is too heavy.

Tested (confirmed): The southern path likely leads to another underground region but requires a reliable light source. -> The southern Dam route reaches Deep Canyon and subsequently darker regions; the carried lantern was insufficient after prolonged travel, and inadequate light caused death.
The studio contains an open, decorated door at its south end, and the room description indicates it is associated with a chimney route.
The troll's first successful sword attack staggers it; a later slash misses, and a subsequent sword attack kills it.
After the troll dies, the sword loses its glow and the troll's carcass disappears; eastward passage is then accessible.
The toothpaste-like tube is takeable, but inventory weight can prevent taking it.
The maintenance-room water level rises after many commands and eventually becomes fatal at neck height.
The dam bolt cannot be turned with either the screwdriver or wrench.
The visible control panel and green bubble do not respond specially to examination.
Opening the matchbook reveals five matches, but this transcript does not show a match being lit or providing sustained room illumination.
The west passage cannot be entered by ordinary west movement, and examining it did not reveal a special feature.
The dam's south route leads to Deep Canyon, not to an immediately fatal dark room, when the lantern is still usable.
The platinum bar is present on the ground after returning from Damp Cave, but taking it produces only 'bar bar ...'.
Rule: Inventory load can prevent taking objects until carried items are dropped.
Rule: Repeated actions and movement can advance environmental hazards, and excessive exposure can kill the player.
Rule: A route may be available only after defeating a hostile blocker.
Rule: Some commands require an explicit object or tool; an incomplete command does not perform the intended action.
Rule: Ordinary movement can fail at apparent passages that require a special interaction.
The gate cannot be opened or passed while protected by an invisible force; ordinary opening, touching, giving an object, and moving south do not bypass it.
The mirror can be broken with the sword, after which it remains broken; using a knife or screwdriver does not provide an additional result.
The cave's downward staircase leads to Entrance to Hades, but repeated travel between the cave and Hades did not reveal a way past the gate.
The brass lantern eventually becomes insufficient for this route; after prolonged repeated travel, the game warned that more light was needed and death by a grue followed.
The tube is Frobozz Magic Gunk, but this run did not successfully give it to the thief or demonstrate a use on the dam bolt.
The water hazard continues rising after actions and reaches dangerous levels; reducing inventory and leaving the room avoids immediate drowning in this run.
The thief can appear while the player is exploring the underground passages, carrying a large bag, but the attempted command 'observe thief' is not recognized.
Rule: Extended repeated movement and activity consume the brass lantern until it becomes unsafe for dark-area travel.
Rule: An invisible force can block a route or object interaction even when the destination or object is visibly present.
Rule: Using a specific object can be required for combat or destruction actions; incomplete commands prompt for the missing object.
Rule: A hostile or hazardous underground area can remain survivable for a while but become fatal when the relevant resource is exhausted.
Taking the screwdriver is possible after reducing inventory load; the thief may leave while stealing possessions.
The chimney cannot be climbed while carrying objects, and attempting it empty-handed only gives a warning rather than ascent.
The studio can serve as a persistent cache for dropped objects; returning revealed many previously carried objects there.
Breaking the mirror with the sword permanently breaks it and produces a luck warning, but no passage south becomes available.
The painting is no longer present after it was taken and later dropped elsewhere; attempting to take it again fails.
The thief can steal the player's possessions when the player handles objects near him.
The sword's glow can return after underground travel, but it can later disappear again during exploration.
Moving west from the gallery enters an unlit dark place; moving there without sufficient light causes grue death.
Rule: Inventory load can block object-taking and movement-based actions, while dropping objects can make them possible.
Rule: Darkness can kill even after entering a dark area if the player continues without adequate light.
Rule: Dropped objects remain available in rooms and can be encountered on later visits.
Rule: Hostile thieves can steal carried possessions when the player interacts with objects near them.

Experiment: holding bottle, died, garlic, knife, leaflet, light, lunch, manual, sack, sword, tube, water, `examine tube` -> "---> Frobozz Magic Gunk Company <--- All-Purpose Gunk The water level here is now up to your knees. The thief knocks you out. The thief, forgetting his essentia" [score 44->34] (you died)
The brass lantern grows dim during repeated movement; when nearly out, the game warns that more light is needed for northwest travel, and retreating north leads to grue death.
The beach's westward tight passage cannot be entered using ordinary movement or the attempted commands tested in this run.
The command to kill the troll requires an explicit weapon; after the incomplete command, the game prompted for one.
The sword's glow can be absent after entering from the cellar and later returns when returning north from East of Chasm.
Examining the bottle confirms it contains water while underground at the beach.
Rule: Extended movement and actions consume the carried lantern, eventually making dark-area travel unsafe.
Rule: Insufficient light can cause grue death even when attempting to retreat from a dark route.
Rule: Some apparent passages require a special interaction rather than ordinary movement, and unsupported commands may be rejected.

Experiment: holding bottle, died, garlic, knife, leaflet, light, lunch, manual, sack, sword, tube, water, `pour water on brown button` -> "The water spills over the brown button, to the floor, and evaporates. The water level here is now up to your knees. The thief knocks you out. The thief, forgett" [score 44->34] (you died)
Opening the matchbook reveals five matches, but lighting a match requires carrying the matchbook; after lighting, moving south caused the match to go out.
The matchbook can be taken only after reducing inventory load; carrying too much prevented taking it.
Breaking the mirror with the sword does not open the southern route; the south exit remains impassable.
After the troll is defeated, returning later reveals the bloody axe, but it may be too heavy to take while carrying the current inventory.
The thief appears in the Troll Room after following the underground route and kills the player when attacked with the sword.
The beach route is accessible with the lantern still on, but the explored north-south movement does not reveal another route; west returns to Damp Cave.
The round room's northeast direction is blocked, despite the room having passages in many directions.
Rule: Inventory load can prevent taking objects, and dropping an item can make a later pickup possible.
Rule: Hostile characters can make attacking them immediately fatal, even when the player has the sword.

Tested (refuted): They may provide short-lived light for a dark route or ignite another object. -> The matchbook does provide a short-lived burning match, but the attempted route test did not show useful sustained illumination.
A skeleton key can be taken from the skeleton area and has no special property when examined; its use remains unresolved.
A leather bag of coins can be taken from the skeleton area, awarding 10 points.
The rusty knife can be taken after reducing inventory load; examining it reveals nothing special.
The skeleton area contains a useless lantern, a rusty knife, a skeleton key, and an old leather bag of coins.
The Maze's downward route cannot be used to return upward; after descending, upward movement can fail.
The thief can appear in the maze and is associated with a large bag, but this run did not test a successful interaction with him.
The gate remains impassable despite being visibly open; touching or examining it reveals protection by an invisible force.
The dome's lower room cannot be reached by ordinary downward movement; the railing and dome revealed nothing special, and throwing commands were unrecognized.
When the brass lantern burned out, the player could neither light it nor take the nearby sack because the area was too dark, and continued movement caused grue death.
Rule: An exhausted lantern cannot be relit, and darkness can prevent taking visible objects before causing grue death.
Rule: The game awards substantial score for collecting certain treasures, not merely for entering rooms.
Rule: Specific object interactions must use command forms recognized by the parser; unsupported forms do not perform the intended action.
Rule: Inventory reduction can enable taking objects that previously exceeded the load limit.
Rule: Some hostile characters can appear unexpectedly while exploring and may steal possessions rather than being safely attackable.

hyps.name: leaflet
hyps.hypothesis: It may provide introductory information or instructions.
hyps.test: read leaflet

hyps.name: brown sack
hyps.hypothesis: It stores food or other useful supplies.
hyps.test: open sack; examine sack
hyps.conclusion: The sack stores food and garlic.

hyps.name: lunch
hyps.hypothesis: It may serve as food or a survival item.
hyps.test: eat lunch

hyps.name: clove of garlic
hyps.hypothesis: It may protect against or affect a creature encountered later.
hyps.test: carry garlic and use it near a hostile creature

hyps.name: bottle of water
hyps.hypothesis: It may be needed to drink or solve a later environmental problem.
hyps.test: take bottle; use or pour water at a later obstacle

hyps.name: dark staircase
hyps.hypothesis: It leads to unexplored areas but requires a light source.
hyps.test: carry a working light source, then go up
hyps.conclusion: A working lantern permits safe progression up the dark staircase into the attic.

hyps.name: wooden door with strange gothic lettering
hyps.hypothesis: It may be an entrance to another area, currently nailed shut.
hyps.test: examine door; try open door or un-nail door

hyps.name: trophy case
hyps.hypothesis: It may contain or require valuable trophies for score or progression.
hyps.test: examine trophy case; open trophy case

hyps.name: large oriental rug
hyps.hypothesis: It may conceal a trapdoor or other hidden feature.
hyps.test: examine rug; move rug
hyps.conclusion: The rug conceals a trap door leading to the cellar.

hyps.name: Great Canyon
hyps.hypothesis: The canyon may provide a route to unexplored areas via its ledges or river.
hyps.test: explore from Rocky Ledge with down or other available directions

hyps.name: grue
hyps.hypothesis: A hostile creature kills players who travel through darkness without adequate light.
hyps.test: enter the dark place with a lit lamp
hyps.conclusion: The dark staircase area is dangerous without adequate light, while the lit lantern enabled passage.

hyps.name: lamp
hyps.hypothesis: A lamp may illuminate the dark staircase area, but none was available in this route.
hyps.test: find or take a lamp before going up, then use light lamp
hyps.conclusion: The brass lantern permits safe travel up the dark staircase into the attic.

hyps.name: coil of rope
hyps.hypothesis: It may enable descent, climbing, or crossing a dangerous vertical area.
hyps.test: take rope; carry rope to the dome, chasm, or another vertical obstacle; use rope or throw rope

hyps.name: nasty-looking knife
hyps.hypothesis: It may serve as a weapon or tool after the sword disappears.
hyps.test: take knife; use knife against a hostile creature or on a barrier

hyps.name: troll
hyps.hypothesis: It blocks passage and must be defeated to reach the underground passages.
hyps.test: kill troll with sword
hyps.conclusion: Repeatedly killing the troll with the sword defeats it and permits eastward progress.

hyps.name: bloody axe
hyps.hypothesis: It may be a weapon or useful tool after the troll is defeated.
hyps.test: take axe; examine axe; use axe on a barrier
hyps.conclusion: The axe is a takeable object left by the troll, but no special function was observed.

hyps.name: trap door
hyps.hypothesis: It provides access to the cellar and deeper underground areas.
hyps.test: move rug; open trap door; go down

hyps.name: cellar
hyps.hypothesis: It is the entry point to the troll room and lower underground network.
hyps.test: go north from the cellar

hyps.name: flood control buttons
hyps.hypothesis: They may control the dam or water level and reveal a route when used in the right sequence.
hyps.test: press blue button; press yellow button; press brown button; press red button; then inspect the dam

hyps.name: inflatable boat
hyps.hypothesis: It may permit crossing the deep lake or reaching the White Cliffs area.
hyps.test: drop plastic pile; inflate plastic pile with air; enter boat; launch boat

hyps.name: wooden railing
hyps.hypothesis: It may support a safer method of descending into the room below.
hyps.test: examine railing; take railing; use rope at railing; climb railing

hyps.name: tight passage
hyps.hypothesis: It may require a special action or object to enter rather than the command 'enter passage'.
hyps.test: examine passage; enter tight passage; use boat at passage

hyps.name: southern crack
hyps.hypothesis: It may be traversable by a small creature or after transforming/shrinking the player.
hyps.test: enter crack; go south; use a relevant small object or creature at the crack

hyps.name: engraved walls
hyps.hypothesis: The engravings may provide a clue or password for another puzzle.
hyps.test: examine engravings; read engravings

hyps.name: seedy-looking individual
hyps.hypothesis: He may steal valuables and could be encountered again with a way to recover them.
hyps.test: wait in the Round Room; follow him; confront or give him an object

hyps.name: brown button
hyps.hypothesis: It may be part of a multi-button sequence controlling flooding or another mechanism.
hyps.test: press brown button; inspect the water level and dam afterward

hyps.name: elvish sword
hyps.hypothesis: A weapon used to defeat underground enemies.
hyps.test: take sword; kill troll with sword
hyps.conclusion: The elvish sword defeats the troll after repeated attacks and enables access eastward.

hyps.name: East-West Passage
hyps.hypothesis: A route toward deeper areas via the northern stairway.
hyps.test: enter from Troll Room; go north; go down

hyps.name: Reservoir South
hyps.hypothesis: A junction leading to the dam and canyon routes.
hyps.test: go east; go west; go southeast
hyps.conclusion: The explored underground junction connects reservoir, dam, and canyon routes.

hyps.name: Stream View
hyps.hypothesis: The small stream opening may be accessible to a smaller object or creature.
hyps.test: examine opening; try enter stream opening; use an appropriate small object

hyps.name: Dam Lobby
hyps.hypothesis: A hub for accessing private dam rooms and possibly useful documents or controls.
hyps.test: go north; go east; examine and take guidebooks or matchbook

hyps.name: thief
hyps.hypothesis: A dangerous guardian carrying a valuable large bag; it may require a nonviolent solution or a different weapon.
hyps.test: avoid attacking; observe thief; try give or use an appropriate item

hyps.name: large bag
hyps.hypothesis: The thief's valuable contents may be needed for further progress.
hyps.test: deal with thief without attacking, then take bag; examine bag

hyps.name: Frobozz Magic Gunk
hyps.hypothesis: A tool or consumable that may affect machinery or barriers.
hyps.test: take tube; examine tube; apply gunk to dam controls or another object

hyps.name: painting of unparalleled beauty
hyps.hypothesis: It may be a valuable treasure or an object that can be vandalized, taken, or otherwise interacted with.
hyps.test: examine painting; take painting; vandalize painting

hyps.name: paper congratulating the player
hyps.hypothesis: It may be collectible text or a humorous reward with no mechanical use.
hyps.test: read paper; examine paper; take paper
hyps.conclusion: The studio paper is collectible and can be read; it identifies the player as the owner of ZORK I.

hyps.name: matchbook
hyps.hypothesis: It may provide matches or a clue connected to the dam and possibly serve as a light-related tool.
hyps.test: take matchbook; open matchbook; examine matchbook; light matchbook
hyps.conclusion: The matchbook contains matches and can light a match, but the transcript does not show it providing sustained area illumination.

hyps.name: guidebooks
hyps.hypothesis: They may contain a clue about the dam's controls or hidden routes.
hyps.test: read guidebooks; take guidebooks; examine guidebooks

hyps.name: river Frigid
hyps.hypothesis: It may provide a route or interact with a boat, but the transcript does not establish a crossing.
hyps.test: examine river; enter river; launch boat; go along river

hyps.name: scramble down at dam
hyps.hypothesis: It may provide access to additional areas around or beyond the river.
hyps.test: down; scramble down; examine scramble

hyps.name: flood control dam #3
hyps.hypothesis: A major underground landmark with routes to the dam base, lobby, and dark southern area; its controls may be needed for deeper progress.
hyps.test: examine sluice gates; examine control panel; push blue button; push yellow button; push red button

hyps.name: rising water
hyps.hypothesis: The leak may eventually force evacuation or serve as a timed environmental puzzle.
hyps.test: wait; examine water; search room; try south; try east

hyps.name: pile of plastic
hyps.hypothesis: It may be the inflatable boat or another usable plastic object, despite having no obvious features when examined.
hyps.test: take pile; inflate pile; examine pile; open pile

hyps.name: dark southern route from Dam
hyps.hypothesis: The southern path likely leads to another underground region but requires a reliable light source.
hyps.test: light lantern; south; go south with lantern; return north before the lantern dims
hyps.conclusion: The southern Dam route reaches Deep Canyon and subsequently darker regions; the carried lantern was insufficient after prolonged travel, and inadequate light caused death.

hyps.name: water-level controls
hyps.hypothesis: The buttons may alter flooding and eventually open or close routes elsewhere in the dam complex.
hyps.test: push brown button; push blue button; push yellow button; push red button; revisit Dam and Reservoir South

hyps.name: chimney from Studio
hyps.hypothesis: It may provide an alternate route upward, but likely requires a specific condition or object rather than merely carrying nothing.
hyps.test: drop every carried object, then enter chimney or climb chimney

hyps.name: thief's theft behavior
hyps.hypothesis: The thief may be a recurring hazard whose behavior can be exploited or prevented to recover a valuable bag or stolen objects.
hyps.test: observe thief; wait; give thief an object; follow thief after he leaves

hyps.name: studio object cache
hyps.hypothesis: Objects left in explored rooms persist and may need to be staged there for a later puzzle.
hyps.test: leave a selected object in Studio, return later, and try the object with the chimney or another barrier

hyps.name: Narrow Passage
hyps.hypothesis: It may connect to unexplored regions beyond the briefly narrowed corridor.
hyps.test: from Round Room, go south; then try south, north, and any visible exits

hyps.name: lean and hungry gentleman
hyps.hypothesis: This may be the thief moving through underground rooms and may interact with valuable objects or inventory.
hyps.test: wait or move between North-South Passage and Deep Canyon, then observe or try giving an object

hyps.name: five matches
hyps.hypothesis: They may provide short-lived light for a dark route or ignite another object.
hyps.test: open matchbook; light match; immediately enter the dark southern dam route
hyps.conclusion: The matchbook does provide a short-lived burning match, but the attempted route test did not show useful sustained illumination.

hyps.name: water level at waist
hyps.hypothesis: The rising water may eventually block or alter the room and may be controlled by the buttons.
hyps.test: wait or perform several actions after pressing blue/yellow/red, and observe whether exits or objects change

hyps.name: cave-ins
hyps.hypothesis: They may block routes that can be opened with a suitable tool or object.
hyps.test: examine cave-ins; try moving toward each blocked direction and use the rope, knife, screwdriver, or wrench

hyps.name: screwdriver
hyps.hypothesis: It may operate or repair a control, panel, or object elsewhere in the underground area.
hyps.test: Take the screwdriver, then try USE SCREWDRIVER ON PANEL and USE SCREWDRIVER ON GREEN BUBBLE at the Dam.

hyps.name: dark west route from Dam
hyps.hypothesis: It may lead to another underground region, but requires a light source already active before entry.
hyps.test: Return with a lit lantern and go WEST from the Dam.

hyps.name: dark south route from Dam
hyps.hypothesis: It may lead to the White Cliffs or another unexplored region and requires a working light.
hyps.test: Return with a lit lantern and go SOUTH from the Dam, then explore and return before the lantern dims.

hyps.name: grue death after retreat
hyps.hypothesis: The dark route remains lethal even when attempting to return, confirming that light must be prepared before entry.
hyps.test: Enter the route only with a lit lantern and compare the result of returning north.

hyps.name: platinum bar
hyps.hypothesis: It may be a treasure or object needed elsewhere, although taking or examining it was not tested in this transcript.
hyps.test: take platinum bar; examine platinum bar; try using it at the cave-ins or dam controls

hyps.name: Damp Cave
hyps.hypothesis: It may provide access through the southern crack or onward east toward the beach.
hyps.test: go east; examine crack; try putting a small object into the crack; continue east

hyps.name: tight passage into White Cliffs
hyps.hypothesis: The west passage may require a specific object or action rather than ENTER or WEST.
hyps.test: examine tight passage; try squeeze through passage; try entering passage with rope, knife, or another small object

hyps.name: lamp exhaustion warning
hyps.hypothesis: The lantern's remaining life is a timed resource, so a fresh or alternate light may be required before entering this route.
hyps.test: restart, minimize movement while carrying the lantern, and leave the beach immediately when it becomes dim; test another light source

hyps.name: sword glow loss
hyps.hypothesis: The sword may have a temporary illumination effect that expires and returns under unknown conditions.
hyps.test: record when the glow disappears; revisit earlier rooms; examine or wait while carrying the sword

hyps.name: open decorated south door
hyps.hypothesis: It may be the object-specific chimney route upward or another connection requiring a special movement command.
hyps.test: drop every carried object; enter chimney; climb chimney; enter south door

hyps.name: toothpaste-like tube
hyps.hypothesis: It may be Frobozz Magic Gunk intended to affect the dam bolt or another mechanism.
hyps.test: take tube; examine tube; use gunk on bolt; put gunk on bolt

hyps.name: drowning threshold
hyps.hypothesis: The room becomes fatal when rising water reaches or passes neck height, so actions must be limited or the leak must be stopped.
hyps.test: press blue; press red; press yellow; press brown; wait; examine water

hyps.name: north-south passage fork
hyps.hypothesis: The passage may provide an unexplored route beyond the fork, possibly toward the thief or deeper underground areas.
hyps.test: from Deep Canyon go southwest; try north; try south; try northeast

hyps.name: platinum bar response
hyps.hypothesis: The repeated 'bar bar ...' response may indicate a special parser interaction or an unresolved treasure behavior rather than a normally collectible bar.
hyps.test: examine bar; take platinum; drop bar; use bar

hyps.name: Entrance to Hades gate
hyps.hypothesis: The invisible force may require a specific object or state, possibly related to the strongly glowing sword or another untested interaction.
hyps.test: examine gate; try push gate; try enter gate; try use sword on gate; try use gunk on gate

hyps.name: mirror
